subject: Request to retain slices for postmortem — Finova Health incident
messages:
From: Tim Carroll <tim.carroll@finovahealth.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Possible data needed for postmortem — request to retain a few days of logs

Hi Redwood team,

We just ran into a throttling-related degradation in our staging run that affected Finova’s ingest pipeline between 04/29 22:10 UTC and 04/30 01:30 UTC. Our SREs would like a short window to inspect request/response slices tied to our tenant (finova-prod-42) while we complete a root-cause analysis.

Can you hold the relevant telemetry and KV cache artifacts for two weeks? We understand there are retention rules — we’re asking for a short, timeboxed exception for debugging only. Happy to sign an NDA or an evidence custody form.

Attachments: finova-debug-snippet-20280429.json (partial traces, redacted)

Thanks,
Tim Carroll
SRE Lead, Finova Health
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Possible data needed for postmortem — request to retain a few days of logs

Markus / Priyom — forwarding Finova’s ask. Customer is requesting a short exception to retention for investigation.

Context: Monica was on the incident call; customer is worried about losing the traces needed for RCA. They explicitly request two weeks. I attached the snippet Tim included.

Questions:
- What is the minimum safe scope we can grant (time range + artifact types) without violating our retention and encryption policy?
- Do we need legal signoff / a written acceptance of liability?

Suggested immediate mitigation: create a timeboxed, access-controlled snapshot export of tenant-scoped logs and redact obvious PII server-side. If compliant, provide SRE access via a gated upload to their secure bucket.

Attachment: customer-incident-summary.docx

—
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-30T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Possible data needed for postmortem — request to retain a few days of logs

Markus / Monica — quick take from ops/legal:

1) Policy baseline: standard tenant telemetry retention is 30 days for logs, 7 days for full request payloads (redacted), and 14 days for metrics. We can’t routinely extend host-level retention without a documented exception and an approval chain.

2) Narrow-scope option (preferred): provide a 7-day hold limited to (a) tenant-scoped request IDs, (b) prefix-truncated request/response headers, and (c) aggregated latency traces. No full payloads. This can be done with minimal policy churn if the customer signs an Acknowledgement (I’ll draft).

3) Full-slice option (requires Ops + Security review): hold full request/response payloads for 14 days in an encrypted bucket with strict KMS key access and audit logging. We’d require a written request on company letterhead + temporary access contract.

Action: Laura — can you confirm whether the KV cache snapshots are allowed to be exported under our current encryption/KMS controls? Also need your view on retention exceptions for SOC2 implications.

Priyom Das
Senior Ops Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Possible data needed for postmortem — request to retain a few days of logs

Thanks — read this morning. Short answers:

- KV cache: we cannot export raw decryption material. Any snapshot must be of application-level artifacts only (request/response slices), and redaction must be applied to PII fields prior to export.
- KMS: we can create a timebound envelope key that is disabled after the hold window. All exports must be encrypted at rest with customer-specific key and access logged.
- SOC2/compliance: a temporary hold itself is acceptable as long as it’s documented, approved, and the scope is minimal. We should not change global retention settings; use isolated snapshot exports in a new, auditable S3 path.

Recommended path: grant the Narrow-scope option (Priyom #2) for 7 days, produce an Acknowledgement template for customer signature, and provision read-only, time-limited access to the export for Finova SREs. If customer insists on full payloads, escalate to Legal + Sales leadership and request company-letterhead + indemnity clause.

I’ve flagged this for the security on-call to assist with the export scripts; they can run the redaction routine and produce an auditable CFN deployment.

—
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Possible data needed for postmortem — request to retain a few days of logs

Thanks team — I approve the Narrow-scope option for Finova Health:
- 7-day hold starting 2028-05-02T16:00:00Z for tenant finova-prod-42
- Export limited to tenant-scoped request IDs, truncated headers, aggregated traces; no full payloads
- Use timebound envelope key and write export to an auditable, customer-specific path
- Monica: get the Acknowledgement signed (I’ll review the draft).
- Priyom: please attach the liability language; Laura: please own the export run and confirmation of redaction prior to handoff.

Monica — communicate the decision to Tim and include the next steps and timeline. If Finova insists on broader data, escalate back to me.

Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success (Interim), Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
